work.problem: KAN-83 item 6 (owner decision 2026-11-24): add .claude/settings.local.json and .env files to the consumer .gitignore baseline every factory repo starts from, propagate it, and scan every factory repo's tracked files and history for exposed credentials.

findings.reason: Long-lived keys: this change adds .gitignore exclusions and scanned every factory repo's history for keys; Gitleaks found no real credential, so nothing to rotate. Its correction (SSO, deny policy) is not reused or touched.
This change adds no journal text and edits none; the journal stays append-only.
Control-catch attribution is untouched; no finding is recorded or attributed by this change.
Board ticket contract; this change touches only .gitignore files and a consumer template.
Branch protection is not changed here; the rulesets stay as they are.
Unrelated to repository exclusions or secrets; nothing in its scope is touched.
Journal CAPA field format; no journal entry is added or edited.

The consumer template is copied, not synced (the sync action vendors .playbook/ only), so the new templates/consumer/.gitignore reaches existing repos only through the per-repo PRs opened with it, not through the sync.
Same sync gap as F-0035: the template change does not propagate by itself; each factory repo gets its own small PR (KAN-83 item 6).

Agent PR identity: 11 of the 14 PRs were opened by ddi-factory; this one (public Playbook) and two others were opened over REST as the owner, labelled Agent-authored and flagged, because the public Playbook cannot call the private workflow.
Dependabot auto-merge autonomy evidence; this change is not a dependency update.
Org Policy dry-run constraints; no governance baseline is touched.
Work tracking: the change cites KAN-83 (item 6), an existing ticket; no new ticket is created.

lessons: Copy the exact .env pattern the factory already uses (.env, .env.*, !.env.example) so tracked sanitized examples stay tracked.
A .gitignore protects nothing already committed: the full-history secret scan is the check that matters, and it ran before the PRs.
uncertainty: The secret scan used Gitleaks' default rules; a credential in a format those rules don't know would not be found.
This record was committed after the first attempt (#120) had already been opened without it; that PR is superseded.
